title: Test Databricks serializer defaults through public save/log, patching the module-level detection
answers: how to test databricks default serialization format
mock databricks runtime in flavor tests
test serialization default without running on databricks
body:
Convention from review comments: helper-only tests (calling _get_default_serialization_format directly) do not prove the default reaches the artifact, dependencies or logged-model telemetry, so they are insufficient on their own.
Test setup: patch the flavor's own is_in_databricks_runtime (e.g. mock.patch("mlflow.sklearn.is_in_databricks_runtime", return_value=True)) and the tracking URI via mock.patch("mlflow.get_tracking_uri", return_value="databricks").
Assert: call public save_model and log_model under both contexts and check the flavor configuration serialization_format and the requirements, not only the helper return value.
Constraints: Pytorch export_model=True must still yield pt2 in the same contexts; LightGBM native Booster needs its own check.
applies: Unit tests for flavor serialization defaults in tests/sklearn, tests/pytorch and tests/lightgbm.
says: Models saved in cloud workspace environments do not use the expected default serialization format.
Logged model artifacts in managed notebooks are missing environment-specific packaging requirements.
Ensure logged models automatically apply the recommended platform format when running in Databricks.
Exported model configurations fail to record the correct storage format during model logging.
search: Testing Databricks default serialization formats requires calling public save_model and log_model while patching the flavor's is_in_databricks_runtime and get_tracking_uri. In tests/sklearn, tests/pytorch, and tests/lightgbm, tests must assert on serialization_format and requirements rather than relying solely on _get_default_serialization_format helper returns. PyTorch export_model=True must still yield pt2 in these contexts, and LightGBM native Booster requires its own check.
